episode.title: Preserve provider HTTP error bodies across heterogeneous SDK error interfaces
episode.before: At parent 5d499272a879398985ad9b1695866ab3d8685053, provider adapters formatted failures independently. Several catch paths returned only Error.message or JSON.stringify(error), hiding HTTP bodies stored in SDK-specific fields; status-aware response adapters still combined status with the opaque message, Bedrock could collapse gateway failures to "Unknown: UnknownError", and the completions adapter appended metadata.raw without a shared duplication check.
episode.after: At merge 6fbeba51af98a37a0695ec8b53308dde81d9ab46, a shared normalizer extracts status and body from known SDK shapes, safely serializes non-Error throws, ignores empty bodies, caps body text at 4000 characters, and records whether the message already contains the body. A shared formatter then exposes status plus body while preserving existing prefixes and avoiding duplicate body text. Eight response, text, and image adapters use this contract; Bedrock retains its exception-category and retention-hint behavior, while the completions path avoids re-appending metadata already present in the normalized body.
episode.diff: Relative to first parent 5d499272a879398985ad9b1695866ab3d8685053, the merge adds packages/ai/src/utils/error-body.ts, replaces local or message-only formatting in eight provider adapters, adds a duplicate guard for metadata.raw, and adds three test files covering normalization/formatting edge cases plus representative text, response, Bedrock, and image-provider catch paths. The implementation diff is 580 insertions and 36 deletions across 12 files.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned ref 6fbeba51af98a37a0695ec8b53308dde81d9ab46 is the merge of PR #5832, titled "fix(ai): surface provider HTTP error body instead of opaque SDK message", with first parent 5d499272a879398985ad9b1695866ab3d8685053 and implementation parent 62fad94f1ab17e94a3f6f8d00ef3bae5cd5f8f66.

Before the change, affected adapters used Error.message, String(error), or JSON.stringify(error); the status-aware OpenAI and Azure helpers included status but still used error.message, and Bedrock derived its core message without inspecting the raw response body.

evidence_units.claim: The new normalization contract probes statusCode, status, $metadata.httpStatusCode, and $response.statusCode; probes string body, non-empty parsed error objects, and $response.body; trims and caps the selected body; safely serializes non-Error values; and records whether the original message already contains the extracted body.
The shared formatter returns the existing message when the body is absent or already represented, preserves an optional adapter prefix and status, and otherwise formats the extracted status and body.

Azure responses, Google generative AI, Google Vertex, OpenAI Codex responses, OpenAI completions, OpenAI responses, and OpenRouter images route caught errors through the shared normalize-and-format contract; the Azure and OpenAI response adapters preserve their existing provider-specific prefixes.
evidence_units.source: git diff 5d499272a879398985ad9b1695866ab3d8685053 6fbeba51af98a37a0695ec8b53308dde81d9ab46 -- packages/ai/src/api/azure-openai-responses.ts packages/ai/src/api/google-generative-ai.ts packages/ai/src/api/google-vertex.ts packages/ai/src/api/openai-codex-responses.ts packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses.ts packages/ai/src/api/openrouter-images.ts

evidence_units.claim: The Bedrock adapter uses normalized status/body as its core diagnostic only when the SDK message does not already carry the body, while retaining exception-name prefixes and the data-retention hint.
The completions adapter appends metadata.raw only when the normalized error message does not already contain that value, preventing duplicate diagnostics.
Unit tests cover four SDK-shaped errors, non-Error throws, empty parsed bodies, bounded truncation, message/body deduplication, prefix preservation, and status-plus-body formatting.

An image-provider regression test injects an opaque 403 SDK message with a parsed body and requires the returned error to contain both status and gateway reason rather than equal the opaque SDK message.
Representative integration tests exercise a body-blind text adapter, a status-aware response adapter, and Bedrock; they also require metadata.raw to occur exactly once.
The first-parent implementation diff changes 12 files with 580 insertions and 36 deletions, including one shared utility, eight adapter integrations, and three new test files.

candidate_atomics.name: normalize-heterogeneous-provider-failures
candidate_atomics.description: Convert heterogeneous thrown provider values into one bounded diagnostic record containing the original message, optional HTTP status, optional body, and a flag indicating whether the message already carries that body.

semantic_action.intent: Recover actionable HTTP failure details that provider SDKs retain outside Error.message.
semantic_action.pre_state: A provider call has thrown an unknown value whose status and body may occupy SDK-specific fields or whose message may already contain the body.
semantic_action.post_state: The failure is represented by a stable record with a safe message, optional numeric status, optional non-empty bounded body, and an explicit body-in-message predicate.
semantic_action.validation: Synthetic error shapes verify field precedence and extraction for multiple SDK conventions, non-Error serialization, empty-body handling, truncation, and existing-body detection.

candidate_atomics.name: compose-nonduplicating-provider-diagnostic
candidate_atomics.description: Render a normalized failure so status and body are exposed when available while preserving prefixes, fallbacks, and messages that already contain the body.

semantic_action.intent: Expose the provider's actual HTTP reason without duplicating it or discarding established adapter context.
semantic_action.pre_state: A normalized failure may contain status and body separately, may already include the body in its message, and may require an adapter-specific prefix.
semantic_action.post_state: The diagnostic contains status plus body when separately available; otherwise it preserves the message, with the requested prefix and status where applicable, and does not print the body twice.
semantic_action.validation: Formatter unit tests assert unprefixed and prefixed status/body output, preservation of messages already containing a body, and fallback behavior for non-Error values.

candidate_atomics.name: adapt-provider-catch-boundaries
candidate_atomics.description: Replace adapter-local message-only formatting with the shared diagnostic contract while retaining adapter-specific semantics such as category prefixes, hints, and supplemental metadata.

semantic_action.intent: Make provider-facing text, response, streaming, and image entry points consistently return actionable HTTP failure details.
semantic_action.pre_state: Adapter catch blocks independently format thrown SDK values, and some lose bodies or duplicate supplemental details.
semantic_action.post_state: Affected adapters consume the shared normalized diagnostic while preserving their established stop reasons, contextual prefixes, exception categories, hints, and nonduplicated supplemental data.
semantic_action.validation: Mocked end-to-end catch-path tests require status and body propagation for representative image, text, response, and Bedrock tiers and require supplemental raw metadata to appear once.

candidate_atomics.name: validate-provider-diagnostic-contract
candidate_atomics.description: Exercise utility edge cases and representative real adapter catch paths with opaque SDK messages that retain the actual reason in separate body fields.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent regressions where normalization works in isolation but adapter output still hides or duplicates the provider reason.
semantic_action.pre_state: The shared contract and adapter integrations have been implemented, but their behavior across error shapes and adapter tiers is not yet established.
semantic_action.post_state: Tests specify that output preserves error stop state, includes HTTP status and body reason, excludes known opaque-only output, bounds long bodies, and avoids duplicate supplemental text.
semantic_action.validation: The three added test files provide utility-level and representative adapter-level assertions; the available evidence does not include an executed test or CI result.

candidate_workflows.name: surface-hidden-http-error-details-at-provider-boundaries
candidate_workflows.description: Establish one bounded error contract, compose it without duplication, adopt it at affected provider boundaries while preserving local behavior, and verify both utility semantics and representative catch paths.

workflow_graph.goal: Return actionable provider HTTP failure details when an SDK exposes the status and response body outside its opaque Error.message.
workflow_graph.entry_state: Multiple provider adapters own incompatible catch formatting, and gateway or proxy failures can expose only an opaque SDK message even though the thrown object retains a status and body.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Affected adapters expose a bounded status/body diagnostic without double-printing existing content and without losing adapter-specific prefixes, categories, hints, stop reasons, or supplemental metadata.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence establishes extraction only for the implemented SDK field shapes; behavior for other SDK error layouts remains outside this episode.
Only representative adapter tiers have end-to-end regression tests; the other migrated adapters rely on the shared utility contract and analogous call-site integration.
No test execution log or CI status was available, so runtime passage of the added tests is not claimed.
Cross-repository peers, semantic deduplication, pattern induction, and holdout validation are outside this single-episode extraction and remain deferred.

unresolved_questions: The GitHub bundle lacks the PR body, issue discussion, reviews, timeline, and status checks, so the original acceptance discussion and CI result cannot be established.
It is not established from the pinned change whether response bodies can contain sensitive material requiring redaction in addition to the implemented 4000-character cap.
The change intentionally enumerates known SDK field shapes; no evidence establishes a generic fallback for future providers that store status or body under different fields.
